result.rationale: The diff shows zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` as the third arg to refreshOAuthTokens (`"zoho-bigin", credentialId`), while every other call site passes `credential.userId`. refreshOAuthTokens sends it as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` in the sync payload, so the wrong identifier (credential row id) is sent to the credential sync endpoint. This is a real defect in shared-credential mode.

judged_text: The zoho-bigin call site passes credentialId as the third argument of refreshOAuthTokens, whose contract (per every other call site and the sync payload field name calcomUserId) expects the Cal.com user id, so the sync endpoint is asked for credentials belonging to the wrong identity. In shared-credential mode the sync request carries the credential row id as calcomUserId, so the parent application either returns another user's credentials (which get stored under this user's credential) or fails, and the failure is surfaced only as a downstream token-parse error, not as a wrong-identifier error.

In shared-credential mode the sync request carries the credential row id as calcomUserId, so the parent application either returns another user's credentials (which get stored under this user's credential) or fails, and the failure is surfaced only as a downstream token-parse error, not as a wrong-identifier error.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the third parameter is explicitly `userId: number | null` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (via `userId.toString()`). Nearly all updated call sites pass `credential.userId`. However, in `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call is `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`, which is inconsistent and (given the name and surrounding patterns) indicates a credential-row id is being passed where a Cal.com user id is required. This would cause the sync endpoint to be queried with the wrong identity (`calcomUserId`), matching the finding.
